notes:
Shared contract for Raft's first-party action cards (botiverse/slock packages/shared/src/actionCardSpec.ts; this file is pinned by actionCard.v1.vector.sha256). Compare everything as JSON values: key order is irrelevant, and an absent key differs from a null one.
cards[]: parse `card` in read mode (what a client accepts) and in emit mode (what a server may send; clients need not implement it). `read`/`emit` give the verdict. For read: accept, `parsed` is the card after the read parse: defaults filled in (Stack direction column, wrap false; Text tone default, mono false; Badge tone neutral; Notice tone info; Button emphasis secondary); unknown keys dropped (the read rules below), and so are unknown icons and unknown locale keys; unknown action kinds as {kind: unsupported, originalKind}, unknown open intents as {kind: unsupported, originalKind: open, originalIntent}, actions of a known kind with a key that kind does not take as {kind: unsupported, originalKind} (an open: plus originalIntent), unknown field types as {type: unsupported, originalType, name}. `strip[set]` is stripActionCardSpec(parsed, capabilitySets[set]): null without card.v1.
Rejecting a card means the client shows the legacy presentation. The 24576-byte limit is emit only (JSON.stringify of the parsed card, UTF-8); clients do not measure.
Lengths are Unicode code points (an astral emoji is 1). Ids are lowercase canonical UUIDs. Integers are safe integers (|n| <= 2^53 - 1); vectors never write a fraction or an exponent. Timestamps are strict RFC 3339 UTC on a date that exists; Duration compares at millisecond precision. Navigate URLs: https, no user info, no explicit port other than the default, no fragment, a dotted host that is not an IP literal, at most 2000 UTF-16 units (WHATWG URL parsing).
A raw JSON key __proto__, constructor or prototype is refused wherever a card uses names as keys (element ids, confirm and form ids, param names, field names). On an object with fixed keys (the read rules below) such a key is an unknown key like any other.
Templates are read left to right: {{ and }} are a literal brace, {name} a placeholder, any other brace makes the Msg invalid. Every placeholder in every kept locale's template needs a param.
formValues[]: parse `form` as a FormSpec in read mode, then run the value checks in client and in server mode; `client`/`server` are the exact issue lists. At most one issue per field, in field order; then (server) unknown names sorted by UTF-16 code units. Blank = only U+0009-U+000D, U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+FEFF.
messages[]: pick the template for `locale` (else en) and fill in params: strings as is, integers as base-10 digits, EntityRefs as {ref} segments; adjacent text merged, empty text dropped.
schemaVersion 2 (additive over 1): header icons shield and credit_card; Field.clamp (1-6, as Text.clamp); ScopeList.groups (optional, 1-32 unique permission group ids shaped like scope ids; scopes stays required); the Open in web label and the form issue Msgs carry all seven display locales.
Read rules for keys (schemaVersion 3). Each object in a card takes a fixed set of keys: the ones emit accepts. Read drops any other key without looking at its value (it is absent from `parsed`) on: the envelope; every element object (keys besides type, props and, on a Stack, children) and the props of every element type but Button; Msg; EntityRef wherever it appears (EntityRef props, Field value items, Msg params, picker defaults); navigate targets (chosen by kind, so channelId on a channel target is dropped too); trees ({root, elements}: spec, result and each confirm's spec); forms; known form fields; Select options. Known keys keep every rule: a bad or missing one rejects the card. Unchanged: children on an element other than a Stack rejects the card; Msg.text drops only keys shaped like a locale (any other key rejects); records keyed by names (elements, confirms, forms, params) check their keys as names.
Read rules for presses (schemaVersion 3). Unknown keys are dropped, except where they could change what a press does (a Button's props, its action, the confirm it opens): there the button becomes Open in web. Its known keys are checked as usual first (a bad or missing one rejects the card), then its action reads as {kind: unsupported, originalKind: <kind>}, plus originalIntent: <intent> on an open (an action that already reads as unsupported stays as it is); strip makes it open_web. (1) Button props take label, emphasis, action, disabledReason. (2) Each known action kind takes: execute {kind, confirm}; open_form {kind, form}; open {kind, intent, gate}; navigate {kind, target, url}; its known keys are checked exactly as emit checks the action (a gate on another intent, or a target and a url together, reject the card). An open whose intent is a string shaped like ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$ that is no known intent reads as {kind: unsupported, originalKind: open, originalIntent} with every other key ignored, as before. (3) A confirm takes title, confirmLabel, spec (its spec keeps the tree and element rules). One with any other key is, once the rest of the card is valid, removed from confirms (which stays, possibly empty), and every execute button in spec naming it reads as unsupported. The tree rules (at most one execute in spec, destructive only on an execute with a confirm, result buttons only navigate or open feedback_ticket, feedback_ticket only in a result) and the confirm and form references see the markers from (1) and (2): such a marker may be destructive, does not count as the card's execute, may be in a result tree, and its confirm or form id is not looked up. (3) comes last and changes no verdict.
schemaVersion 3 (over 2): the two read rules above; emit is unchanged. Read verdicts changed from reject to accept: msg_values_fallback_gone, unknown_element_prop, toggle_required, field_help_renamed, field_unknown_prop (the key is dropped); button_variant_prop and execute_unknown_prop (the button's action reads as unsupported). New: the read_drops_* and read_unknown_prop_* cases.
schemaVersion 4 (additive over 3): intent feedback_ticket and capability intent.feedback_ticket (in capabilitySets all and each all-but-one set). An open with that intent is allowed in a result tree, and only there: in spec it rejects the card, and in a result an open with any other intent still does. It views the sender's ticket from the done card's metadata.result (product-feedback: ticketId, source); the card carries no ticket id. A reader without the capability strips it to open_web like any intent; one that does not know the intent reads it as unsupported first. New: result_open_feedback_ticket, spec_open_feedback_ticket, result_open_other_intent, read_unknown_intent_in_result, read_unknown_prop_spec_feedback_ticket.
schemaVersion 5 (additive over 4): intent add_seats and capability intent.add_seats (in capabilitySets all and each all-but-one set): a seat request's owner flow (a seats:add card a person sends an owner, task #10). An open with that intent goes in spec, as the other dialog intents. A reader without the capability strips it to open_web like any intent; one that does not know the intent reads it as unsupported first. New: open_add_seats.
schemaVersion 6 (additive over 5): Stack.role. An optional Stack prop, `reason` or `actions`, saying what the Stack is so a client can draw it as that part of its card: `reason` on a column is the agent's own words (an optional muted label Text, then the note Text: the web draws it as its hint; a reason that is not one or two Texts is drawn as the plain column), `actions` on a row is the card's buttons (its actions row). Emit refuses any other value and a role on the other direction (reason on a row, actions on a column); read drops such a role, as an unknown icon, and keeps the Stack. A reader that does not know the prop drops it (read rule for unknown keys), so older clients render the card as before. New: stack_roles, stack_role_unknown, stack_role_wrong_direction. schemaVersion 7: forms[].submitLabels (optional), the submit label per value of one Select of the form; emit checks it names a Select of the form and only its options, read keeps it as it is, and a client without it shows submitLabel. schemaVersion 8 (additive over 7; the question card): (1) the field type Choice and capability field.choice (in capabilitySets all and each all-but-one set; new set no_choice is all without it): {type: Choice, name, label, placeholder?, description?, required?, multiple, minItems?, maxItems?, options: [{value, label: Msg, description?: Msg}] (1-32, values unique, shaped like Select's, never "other"), other?: {label: Msg, description?: Msg, placeholder?: Msg, maxLength 1-500}, default?: {selected, other?}}. Items are the options plus Other when the Choice has it; a Choice takes minItems..maxItems of them when multiple (default 1 and all), one when single; minItems/maxItems only on a multiple one, within the items, minItems <= maxItems; a default selects options once each, writes other only with Other (non-blank, within maxLength) and chooses no more than the Choice takes. Read drops unknown keys on it, its options, its other and its default; a reader without field.choice (and an older one, which reads Choice as an unknown field type) strips the form's button to open_web. (2) forms[].steps (optional): 2-10 steps {title?: Msg, fields: [field names] (1-12)}, the form's pages in order; fields still lists every field, and there is still one submit. Emit refuses steps that do not name every field exactly once; read drops such steps (one page), and a reader that does not know the key drops it. (3) The Choice value {selected: [option values], other?: string} and the issue code too_few ({min}): checks per Choice, at most one issue, in this order: (server) a value that is not exactly {selected: string[], other?: string}, a repeated value, the reserved value other, other on a Choice without Other, or more than one selected on a single Choice -> invalid_format; required (nothing selected and other absent or blank); too_long (other's code points over Other's maxLength); then, with any item (a non-blank other counts as one): too_many {max} (more than maxItems, or than one when single), too_few {min} (a multiple Choice under minItems); (server) a selected value that is no option -> invalid_option. The client leaves a value of the wrong type to the server. (4) The raw Msg: text someone else wrote (an agent's) goes into a Msg-only slot as {key: actionCard.text.raw, text: {en: "{t}"}, params: {t: <text>}} with the text 1-500 code points; the Msg rules already make it plain text in every locale (messages raw_text*). string | Msg slots are unchanged. New: question_card*, choice_*, read_drops_choice_keys, form_steps_*, raw_text_*; formValues choice_*; messages raw_text*.
schemaVersion 9 (additive over 8): intent migrate_agent and capability intent.migrate_agent (in capabilitySets all and each all-but-one set): the migration dialog for an agent:migrate card's Agent. An open with that intent goes in spec, as the other dialog intents. A reader without the capability strips it to open_web like any intent; one that does not know the intent reads it as unsupported first. New: open_migrate_agent.

cards.name: read_unknown_prop_missing_form

cards.note: schemaVersion 8: the question card (question:ask) as the server builds it, unanswered: For, a Field per question, the reason, Answer Questions opening the form. The form has a single Choice (with Other), a multiple Choice (minItems/maxItems, Other with the agent's placeholder) and a TextArea, paged by steps; every field is still in fields. The agent's text is the raw Msg (key actionCard.text.raw, template {t}) in the form's Msg slots and a plain string in Field values and Text. Other carries only Raft's short label (and the agent's placeholder where it gave one). A reader without field.choice strips the button to open_web (no_choice), as does one without form.v1.
